headline: NCP: Hasina's Delhi press conference threatens Bangladesh's sovereignty
summary: The National Citizen Party (NCP) spokesperson stated that allowing the ousted Prime Minister to speak in India undermines Bangladesh's independence. They also urged the government to address the issue with the Indian High Commissioner.
details: The National Citizen Party (NCP) has declared that allowing Sheikh Hasina, the ousted Prime Minister and president of the banned Awami League, to speak at a press conference in New Delhi, India, poses a threat to Bangladesh's sovereignty.
NCP spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajib Bhuiyan made this statement during an emergency press conference held at the party's office in the capital on Thursday evening.

Bhuiyan further alleged that Sheikh Hasina and the Awami League are making maximum efforts to destroy Bangladesh's sovereignty. He also claimed that cricketer Shakib Al Hasan's presence at the Delhi press conference proves his "deep involvement in genocide."
The NCP spokesperson urged the government to be more proactive regarding the matter and suggested that the Indian High Commissioner in Dhaka should be summoned and warned by the government.
caption:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) claims Sheikh Hasina's recent press conference in New Delhi threatens Bangladesh's sovereignty.

The National Citizen Party (NCP) has declared that allowing Sheikh Hasina, the ousted Prime Minister and president of the banned Awami League, to speak at a press conference in New Delhi, India, poses a threat to Bangladesh's sovereignty.

NCP spokesperson Asif Mahmud Sajib Bhuiyan made this statement during an emergency press conference held at the party's office in the capital on Thursday evening.

Bhuiyan further alleged that Sheikh Hasina and the Awami League are making maximum efforts to destroy Bangladesh's sovereignty. He also claimed that cricketer Shakib Al Hasan's presence at the Delhi press conference proves his "deep involvement in genocide."

The NCP spokesperson urged the government to be more proactive regarding the matter and suggested that the Indian High Commissioner in Dhaka should be summoned and warned by the government.

headline_marked: [[SC scraps bail of ex-Army member Hafizur]] in Tonu murder case, orders surrender within 24 hours
headline: SC scraps bail of ex-Army member Hafizur in Tonu murder case, orders surrender within 24 hours
summary: The Supreme Court's Chamber Judge cancelled the High Court bail granted to Hafizur Rahman, the sole accused in the decade-old murder of college student Sohagi Jahan Tonu, following public outcry.
details: The Supreme Court's Chamber Judge has cancelled the bail granted by the High Court to former army member Hafizur Rahman, the sole accused in the murder case of college student Sohagi Jahan Tonu. The court has ordered him to surrender within 24 hours.

Justice Md Rezaul Haque of the Appellate Division's Chamber Court issued this order on Thursday. Earlier, on August 2, a High Court bench had granted bail to Hafizur Rahman, leading to his release from Cumilla Central Jail on August 4 evening.

The decision to grant bail sparked significant criticism on social media, prompting the state to file an appeal with the Chamber Court seeking its cancellation. The court heard the appeal and subsequently revoked the bail.

The order also states that if Hafizur Rahman fails to surrender voluntarily within the stipulated 24 hours, police will be instructed to arrest him. This development marks a significant turn in the long-running case.

Hafizur Rahman was arrested by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) on April 22 this year from his residence in Keraniganj, Dhaka, after a decade since Tonu's murder. He was then placed on a three-day remand for interrogation before being sent to jail.
